name: Database Management Systems (DBMS)

topics.why: 29 questions (21%) in 11 of 15 papers; recurring passage sets (X/Y joins Dec 2023, sailors Sep 2022).
what_to_study: Terminology: degree=attributes, cardinality=tuples, candidate/alternate/super/foreign key definitions
Join tuple counts: cross product n1*n2, natural join max n1*n2, outer joins keep unmatched tuples
Set operations (union, intersection, difference) and reading output to name the operator
Relational division for 'all' queries (pi(eid,cid)/pi(cid))
Writing/validating RA expressions on sailors-reserves-boats (difference for 'not', intersection for 'and')
Referential integrity: which insert/delete violates FK; RA and safe TRC/DRC equal power

topics.why: 28 questions (20% of unit), in 14 of 15 papers, and denser in 2023-25 than before. The single biggest scoring block.
what_to_study: Attribute closure X+ and finding all candidate keys (attributes never on any RHS must be in every key)
Minimal/canonical cover: split RHS, remove extraneous LHS attributes, remove redundant FDs
Highest normal form: partial dependency (2NF), transitive/non-prime RHS (3NF), non-superkey determinant (BCNF)
Lossless-join test (R1 intersect R2 determines R1 or R2) and dependency preservation of a decomposition
Property statements: BCNF => 3NF => 2NF; BCNF may lose dependency preservation; 3NF decomposition always lossless + dependency preserving
Match lists: 1NF atomic, 2NF partial, 3NF transitive, BCNF superkey, 4NF MVD, 5NF join dependency

topics.why: 24 questions (17%) in 11 of 15 papers; fewer in 2023-25 but steady Must by volume.
what_to_study: DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) vs DML (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) classification
GROUP BY / HAVING / aggregate query result reading (row counts, WHERE vs HAVING)
Nested subqueries: ALL, IN, EXISTS, correlated count for top-k
COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col) vs COUNT(DISTINCT col)
UPDATE with subquery, ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN CASCADE/RESTRICT, DROP TABLE
varchar vs char storage

topics.why: 17 questions (12%) in 12 of 15 papers and clearly rising: 1.5 per recent paper vs 0.9 earlier.
what_to_study: Conflict operation definition, conflict vs view serializability, precedence graph cycle test
Protocol properties: 2PL (may deadlock), strict 2PL (cascadeless), conservative 2PL (deadlock-free), timestamp ordering (deadlock-free), Thomas write rule (view only), tree protocol (deadlock-free)
Phantom problem: caused by inserts; handled by index/predicate locking
ACID properties, atomicity and temporary inconsistency, transaction states
Concurrency anomalies: dirty read, lost update, unrepeatable read; recoverable vs irrecoverable schedules

topics.why: 13 questions in 10 of 15 papers (67%) and appearing every recent year; easy marks.
what_to_study: Design phase order: requirements, conceptual, logical, physical
ER attribute kinds (composite, multivalued, derived, complex) and ER vs relational difference
ER-to-relational mapping and minimum tables count (multivalued attribute and M:N get own tables)
Cardinality reading from scenario text; many-to-one as FD Pk(r1)->Pk(r2)
Specialization constraints (total/partial, disjoint/overlapping); ER symbols

topics.why: 11 questions in 9 of 15 papers (60%); mostly one-line concept recall.
what_to_study: DBMS components: query optimizer, transaction processing, buffer/file manager, query processing step order
Authorization/privileges: grant only on own relations, system error is not malicious
Triggers execute automatically; DBMS vs file-system drawbacks; hierarchical/network models have parent-child links
Log-based recovery: undo uncommitted, redo committed
Integrity enforced by schema constraints

topics.why: 10 questions in 7 of 15 papers; all single-fact recall, fewer in recent papers.
what_to_study: Hadoop: NameNode master, DataNode worker; HDFS, MapReduce, HBase, Hive, Pig (Yahoo), Hive (Facebook), Kafka (LinkedIn), Mahout
Fact table holds measures; dimension tables hold descriptors
Data scrubbing/cleaning improves quality; warehouse stores summary data
NoSQL stores: Memcached, CouchDB, graph DBs; k-means minimises within-cluster variance

topics.why: Only 6 questions in 5 papers, and 1 per recent paper pace is low; the order-calculation questions are the only real pattern.
what_to_study: B+ tree leaf order: floor((B - block ptr)/(key + record ptr))
B-tree internal/leaf order with 1024-byte block (57,53 answer convention)
Clustering index on non-key ordering field; dense index entry per search key
Unclustered B+ sorted retrieval cost is about one I/O per record

clusters.title: Candidate keys of U,V,W,X,Y,Z schema
clusters.technique: Z and Y never appear on any RHS so are in every key; add one of U/V/X (they determine each other cyclically) and verify closure.

clusters.title: Key of R(A,B,C,D,F) with C->F, E->A, EC->D, A->B
clusters.technique: E and C never on RHS, so EC is in every key; EC+ = ABCDEF.
clusters.what_changes: Only attribute name E/F vs typo; options identical.

clusters.title: Candidate keys via attribute closure
clusters.technique: Find attributes not on any RHS, start from them, compute closure, then try minimal additions.
clusters.skip_note: Same closure procedure; one worked example gives the method.

clusters.title: Minimal cover / redundant FD
clusters.technique: Split RHS to single attributes, remove extraneous LHS attributes, drop FDs derivable from the rest (A->D from A->BC, BC->D).
clusters.what_changes: FD set; ask for cover or for the redundant FD.

clusters.title: Highest normal form of relation from FDs
clusters.technique: Find keys, flag partial dependencies (not 2NF), then non-prime transitive or non-superkey determinants (not 3NF/BCNF).

clusters.title: Lossless join and dependency preservation of decomposition
clusters.technique: Chase/common-attribute test for lossless; project FDs and check each FD is derivable in union of fragments.

clusters.title: Normal form property statements (BCNF/3NF/4NF)
clusters.technique: Remember BCNF stronger than 3NF; BCNF may not preserve dependencies; 3NF always lossless+dependency preserving; two-attribute relation is BCNF.
clusters.what_changes: Which of the true/false statements is picked.

clusters.title: Match normal forms with properties
clusters.technique: 1NF scalar, 2NF partial, 3NF transitive, BCNF all determinants keys (not always dep preserving), 4NF MVD, 5NF JD.

clusters.title: RA vs relational calculus expressive power
clusters.technique: Basic RA, safe TRC and safe DRC are equivalent in power.

clusters.title: Dec 2023 passage on relations X and Y joins
clusters.technique: Compute matching on S column; natural join and equi-join counts matched tuples, cross product 4x4, right outer keeps all Y, full outer keeps all of both.
clusters.skip_note: Same data; understanding one table solves all.

clusters.title: Sailors-Reserves-Boats relational algebra queries
clusters.technique: Join through Reserves; difference for "not", intersection of sid sets for "and".
clusters.what_changes: Colour, age filters, which query is valid.

clusters.title: Relational division for "all"
clusters.technique: pi(x,y)(R) / pi(y)(S) gives x related to every y.

clusters.title: Candidate/alternate key definitions
clusters.technique: Candidate key = minimal super key (unique and irreducible); alternate = candidate not chosen as primary.

clusters.title: Foreign key and referential integrity
clusters.technique: Foreign key refers to primary key; insert into referencing or delete from referenced violates.

clusters.title: Set operations in relational algebra
clusters.technique: Union, intersection, difference, Cartesian product are set operations; intersection is common tuples.

clusters.title: Degree and cardinality terminology
clusters.technique: Degree = number of attributes; cardinality = number of tuples; cross product degree adds, tuples multiply.

clusters.title: Relational model structure features
clusters.technique: Data in tables of rows and columns; atomic values, supports associations, no complex types.

clusters.title: Nested subquery ALL / EXISTS / correlated
clusters.technique: Translate ALL as every, EXISTS as at least one; correlated count(higher price) < k gives top k.

clusters.title: GROUP BY / HAVING / aggregate result
clusters.technique: Join first, group, then HAVING filters groups; WHERE filters rows.

clusters.title: Nov 2020 EMPLOYEE passage
clusters.technique: Read the schema, DISTINCT with IN, missing join condition gives Cartesian product, ALTER DROP, UPDATE with subquery.

clusters.title: COUNT queries over orders
clusters.technique: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) for distinct customers; COUNT(order_id) for orders of one customer.

clusters.title: DDL vs DML classification
clusters.technique: CREATE/ALTER/DROP are DDL; SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are DML.

clusters.title: SQL command capabilities (INSERT, DROP, modify)
clusters.technique: INSERT adds one or many tuples, UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT modify data, SELECT does not, DROP TABLE removes a relation.

clusters.title: Precedence graph conflict serializability
clusters.technique: Draw edge Ti->Tj for earlier conflicting op; cycle means not conflict serializable; timestamp order gives the serial order.

clusters.title: Concurrency protocol properties
clusters.technique: 2PL may deadlock; strict 2PL cascadeless; conservative 2PL and timestamp deadlock-free; Thomas write view-only; tree protocol deadlock-free.

clusters.title: Conflict and view serializability definitions
clusters.technique: Conflict: different transactions, same item, at least one write; conflict serializable implies view serializable.

clusters.title: Phantom problem
clusters.technique: Caused by inserts; handled by index locking and predicate locking.

clusters.title: ACID and concurrency anomalies
clusters.technique: ACID: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability; uncontrolled concurrency causes dirty read, lost update, incorrect summary.

clusters.title: Database design phase order
clusters.technique: Requirements, conceptual, logical, physical.

clusters.title: ER attribute types and ER vs relational
clusters.technique: Composite divisible, multivalued only in ER, relational attributes atomic.

clusters.title: June 2024 customer-orders ER passage
clusters.technique: Customer 1:N orders, orders hold foreign keys, order-product M:N, rep manages many.

clusters.title: B-tree / B+ tree order from block size
clusters.technique: Solve p*ptr + key sizes <= block size.

clusters.title: DBMS components and query processing
clusters.technique: Optimizer reorders operations; transaction manager ensures consistent concurrent execution; scan-parse-validate, optimize, generate code, run.

clusters.title: Authorization and privileges
clusters.technique: Privileges can be granted only on own relations; OS authorization has drawbacks.

clusters.title: File system drawbacks and DB models
clusters.technique: Redundancy, inconsistency, isolation, atomicity issues; hierarchical/network have parent-child.

clusters.title: Hadoop and big data ecosystem facts
clusters.technique: NameNode master; HBase, Hive, MapReduce, Pig, Kafka; NoSQL stores.

clusters.title: Data warehouse terminology
clusters.technique: Fact table holds measures; scrubbing cleans data; summary data.

examiner_mindset: Normalization is the biggest bloc and rising; he reuses the same FD schemas verbatim (U,V,W,X,Y,Z keys in 2020 and 2024; R(A,B,C,D,F) in 2023 and 2025).
Passage sets (Q96-Q100 or Q31-Q35) recycle one schema for several questions: X/Y joins, sailors, university schema, customer-orders.
Questions are mostly computational reading (closure, keys, joins, group by) or one-line definition recall; hardly any hard design problems.
Statement-combination and match-the-following options dominate theory topics; distractors swap a true pair (e.g. BCNF vs 3NF dependency preservation).
He reuses definitions in different words: design phases, phantom problem, Hadoop tools, candidate key all recur.
Trap: dependency preservation is guaranteed for 3NF, not BCNF; conflict serializable implies view serializable but not the reverse.
Trap: SELECT is DML but not data modification; COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col); WHERE vs HAVING.
Transactions rising: precedence graph schedules and protocol property matching appear nearly every year.
Indexing and data mining are rarely asked; B+ order calculations appear only occasionally and use simplified arithmetic.
Overlaps with Unit 3/OS-style concurrency and Unit 10 big data only at the keyword level.

formulas.name: Attribute closure
formulas.formula: X+ = X plus attributes derived by repeatedly applying FDs; X is a superkey iff X+ = all attributes
formulas.note: Attributes never on any RHS must be in every key

formulas.name: Candidate key
formulas.formula: Minimal superkey; alternate key = candidate not chosen as primary

formulas.name: Minimal cover
formulas.formula: Single-attribute RHS; no extraneous LHS attribute; no redundant FD
formulas.note: Redundant FD = derivable from the rest

formulas.name: 2NF
formulas.formula: No non-prime attribute depends on a proper subset of a candidate key

formulas.name: 3NF
formulas.formula: For each X->A: X is a superkey or A is prime

formulas.name: BCNF
formulas.formula: For each nontrivial X->A: X is a superkey
formulas.note: BCNF => 3NF => 2NF => 1NF; may lose dependency preservation; any 2-attribute relation is in BCNF

formulas.name: 4NF / 5NF
formulas.formula: 4NF: every nontrivial MVD has a superkey LHS; 5NF: every join dependency is implied by candidate keys

formulas.name: Lossless binary decomposition
formulas.formula: R1 intersect R2 -> R1 or R1 intersect R2 -> R2
formulas.note: Also check each original FD is preserved in some fragment

formulas.name: 3NF guarantee
formulas.formula: 3NF synthesis is always lossless and dependency preserving; BCNF is lossless but may not preserve

formulas.name: Cross product and join size
formulas.formula: Cross product: degree d1+d2, tuples n1*n2; natural join max tuples n1*n2, min 0
formulas.note: Outer joins add unmatched tuples (right outer >= |right relation|)

formulas.name: Relational division
formulas.formula: pi(x,y)(R) / pi(y)(S) gives x paired with every y

formulas.name: Degree and cardinality
formulas.formula: Degree = number of attributes; cardinality = number of tuples

formulas.name: Referential integrity
formulas.formula: Insert into referencing and delete from referenced relation can violate; ON DELETE CASCADE deletes referencing tuples

formulas.name: B+ tree leaf order
formulas.formula: p*(key + record ptr) + block ptr <= B so p = floor((B - Pb)/(K+Pr))
formulas.note: B=1024,K=9,Pr=7,Pb=6 gives 63; key for B-tree item was (57,53)

formulas.name: Conflicting operations
formulas.formula: Different transactions, same item, at least one write
formulas.note: Cycle in precedence graph => not conflict serializable

formulas.name: Serializability hierarchy
formulas.formula: Conflict serializable => view serializable; Thomas write rule only view serializable

formulas.name: Concurrency protocols
formulas.formula: 2PL may deadlock; strict 2PL cascadeless; conservative 2PL and timestamp ordering deadlock-free; tree protocol deadlock-free

formulas.name: Phantom problem
formulas.formula: Caused by insertions; prevented by index locking or predicate locking

formulas.name: ACID
formulas.formula: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
formulas.note: Deadlock-freedom is not part of ACID

formulas.name: Transaction states
formulas.formula: Active -> partially committed -> committed; active/partially committed -> failed -> aborted
formulas.note: From active: partially committed or failed

formulas.name: Irrecoverable schedule
formulas.formula: Tj reads data written by Ti and commits before Ti commits
formulas.note: Cascadeless needs reads only of committed data

formulas.name: DDL vs DML
formulas.formula: DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP; DML: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

formulas.name: WHERE vs HAVING
formulas.formula: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation

formulas.name: COUNT variants
formulas.formula: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) ignores NULL; COUNT(DISTINCT col) counts distinct values
formulas.note: Missing join condition gives Cartesian product (nov2020_q97)

formulas.name: Top-k correlated query
formulas.formula: where (select count(*) from book where price > B.price) < k lists the k most expensive

formulas.name: varchar vs char
formulas.formula: varchar uses actual length; char(n) is padded to n

formulas.name: Hadoop roles
formulas.formula: NameNode = master, DataNode = worker

formulas.name: Design phases
formulas.formula: Requirements, conceptual, logical, physical

formulas.name: ER-to-relational
formulas.formula: Entity -> table; multivalued attribute -> separate table; M:N -> own table; many-to-one r1 to r2: Pk(r1) -> Pk(r2)
